name: Salt River Project
note: One of the first five projects; Roosevelt came back in March 1911 to dedicate the stone dam that carries his name.

name: Truckee-Carson Project (Newlands Project)
note: Derby Dam turned Truckee River water into a canal bound for the Carson desert, and the main Truckee canal was finished in June 1905.

name: Uncompahgre Valley Project
note: Crews bored a tunnel about six miles through solid rock to carry Gunnison River water into the Uncompahgre Valley.
verify: Coordinate is Wikidata's single point for the tunnel; the tunnel runs roughly 6 miles, so confirm which portal the map should mark.

name: Milk River Project
note: This project planned to borrow water from the St. Mary River near Glacier and send it down the Milk River to farms on Montana's Hi-Line.
verify: The St. Mary storage works were authorized separately on 1905-03-25 and later folded into Milk River. Dodson Diversion Dam was finished in January 1910, after TR left office.

name: North Platte Project
note: Pathfinder Dam stores North Platte water in Wyoming, and the Interstate Canal carries it to farms in western Nebraska.
verify: Authorized in 1903 as the 'Sweetwater' project. The acreage shown is the Interstate Canal unit only (1910 report).

name: Shoshone Project
note: A 328-foot concrete arch dam in the canyon above Cody holds the Shoshone River for farms around Powell.
verify: The dam was finished in January 1910 and renamed Buffalo Bill Dam in 1946.

name: Minidoka Project
note: Minidoka Dam on the Snake River was finished in 1906 and created Lake Walcott.

name: Yuma Project
note: Laguna Dam spans the Colorado River above Yuma and was finished in March 1909.
verify: The 'first dam on the lower Colorado' claim should be checked before it goes on the map (Reclamation's Yuma project history).

name: Lower Yellowstone Project
note: A low rock-and-timber weir near Intake, Montana, sends Yellowstone River water to farms reaching into North Dakota.
verify: The dam was finished in January 1910.

name: Belle Fourche Project
note: An earthen dam 115 feet high and more than a mile long on Owl Creek stores Belle Fourche River water for western South Dakota farms.
verify: The dam was about 97 percent finished in June 1910 and completed in 1911.

name: Hondo Project
note: Engineers built a reservoir near Roswell, but the water seeped into the ground, and the project never delivered much.
verify: Date conflict. The 9th Annual Report (1910) chronology gives 1904-09-06, but that is also the bid-opening date. The 6th Annual Report says construction was authorized 1903-11-10, and Reclamation's project history says 'authorized in 1904.' The coordinate is APPROXIMATE (about 10 to 12 miles west/southwest of Roswell, from the report text) and must be checked on a USGS topo map.

name: Boise Project (Payette-Boise)
note: The Boise River Diversion Dam, finished in 1908, sends river water into the New York Canal for the Boise Valley.
verify: Called the Payette-Boise project at the time. Arrowrock Dam came later (1915).

name: Huntley Project
note: Opened on land ceded by the Crow Tribe, this Yellowstone River project east of Billings first delivered water in 1908.
verify: Coordinate is the Wikidata point for the Huntley Project / town area, not the diversion dam itself (about 2 miles above Huntley). Confirm before mapping. The Crow cession tie should be checked in Reclamation's Huntley history.

name: Klamath Project
note: Klamath engineers drained lakebeds and marshes along the Oregon-California line for farmland, and Clear Lake Dam was finished in January 1910.
verify: The acreage is the lower division only. Link River Dam, now the best-known structure, came in 1921; pick the marker structure accordingly.

name: Garden City Project
note: Kansas's only early project pumped groundwater from under the Arkansas River, but farmers stopped paying their charges and the pumps went quiet by 1910.
verify: No dam; the works were a steam power plant and wells near Deerfield, Kansas. The coordinate is APPROXIMATE (Deerfield area) and should be checked.

name: Okanogan Project
note: An earthen dam on Salmon Creek above Okanogan stored water for orchards in north-central Washington.
verify: The dam was 99 percent finished in June 1910.

name: Umatilla Project
note: Cold Springs Dam, finished in June 1908, stores Umatilla River water for farms around Hermiston in northeastern Oregon.

name: Yakima Project (Sunnyside and Tieton units)
note: The government bought and rebuilt the old Sunnyside canal, and its first water reached farms in 1907.
verify: Only the Sunnyside unit (100,000 acres) and Tieton unit (35,000 acres) were authorized on this date. The Wapato unit followed on 1906-06-16. Yakima units were combined into one project on 1909-03-31.

name: Strawberry Valley Project
note: A tunnel about 3½ miles long sends water from the Colorado River basin west to farms around Spanish Fork.
verify: The coordinate is the reservoir centroid, not the original 1913 Strawberry Dam or the tunnel portal. The tunnel was only 26 percent dug in June 1910. The tunnel length ('about 3½ miles' in the 1910 report) should be checked.

name: Williston Project
structure: Williston steam power and pumping plant
note: Steam power pumped Missouri River water uphill to farms around Williston.
verify: No dam. The coordinate is APPROXIMATE (Williston town area).

name: Buford-Trenton Project
structure: Buford-Trenton pumping plant (barge on the Missouri River)
note: A pump on a barge on the Missouri lifted river water about 30 feet into canals near Buford and Trenton, using power sent from Williston.
verify: No dam. The coordinate is APPROXIMATE (Buford area); the barge site has not been confirmed.

name: Carlsbad Project
note: Reclamation bought a struggling private Pecos River canal system and rebuilt Avalon Dam by November 1907.
verify: Two dates appear. The Secretary approved the board's purchase recommendation on 1905-11-28, and the 1910 chronology says construction was authorized 1906-02-24.

name: Sun River Project
note: The first unit was built on the former Fort Shaw military reservation west of Great Falls and first delivered water in 1909.
verify: The 300,000 acres was the planned whole-project total in 1910; the Fort Shaw unit was 16,000 acres. Willow Creek Dam was begun in 1907 and only 10 percent finished in June 1910.

name: Orland Project
note: East Park Dam on Little Stony Creek stored water for the Sacramento Valley's first federal project, around the town of Orland.
verify: East Park Dam was finished in June 1910.

name: Rio Grande Project
note: Roosevelt signed the 1907 law that paid for a big storage dam on the Rio Grande, though most of it was built after he left office.
verify: This is the likely reason the count is 24 and not 25. Congress authorized Engle (Elephant Butte) Dam and appropriated money on 1907-03-04, but the Secretary did not authorize its construction until 1910-05-23. The only Rio Grande work the Secretary approved under TR was the separate Leasburg project (diversion dam at 32.4972, -106.923; authorized 1905-12-02; 25,000 acres; finished 1908). The 160,000 acres is the US share of the full plan and includes Leasburg's 25,000.
